segments: The seventh period.
The Arab kings.
[the incomprehensible ways] of the Creator.
Secondly,
that men and women do not go to the commemoration of the martyrs at this time to be blessed,
but rather to indulge in wantonness and amusements.
Thirdly,
that it is not right to consider those as lost,
for whom the Lord judged that death was better than life (that it was advantageous for them).
For the pagans perish,
and not the believers.
And in that same year, Mas'ud, the great Sultan of Khorasan, died in the city of Hamadan;
and after him reigned his nephew, Malikshah, son of Muhammad;
and his governor was the emir Khasbeg.
And in the year 1465
[1465] of the Greeks,
Mas'ud, the Sultan of Iconium, went down to Cilicia with a large army of Turks.
And when they encamped against Til Hamdun
and pressed it in battle,
the Lord struck them with gnats and flies, a plague resembling that of the Egyptians in the days of Moses the Great.
And in three days the air they breathed became foul,
and they and their horses fell ill.
And when they saw the mortality that had begun among them,
they abandoned all their baggage and fled.
And Thoros and the Armenians came down upon them from the mountains
and slaughtered them until they were weary.
And he also went out against Gabdania, which is Develi,
and plundered the Turks and returned.
And in this year, the Franks captured Ascalon,
according to accurate reckoning.
And it remained with them for thirty-five years,
until Saladin captured it.
And also in that year,
which is the year 548
[548] of the Arabs,
Husam al-Din Timurtash, the lord of Mardin, died;
and after him reigned his son, Najm al-Din Alpi.
This man was at first very harsh towards the Christians,
but at the time of his death he commanded his sons to treat the Christians well,
and not to do them harm.
It is said
that Saint Mor Abai appeared to him in a vision.
And another son of his, Jamal al-Din, gained dominion over Hani;
and the other one, Samsam al-Din, over Dara.
And in the year 1466,
his son Qilij Arslan.
And while he could scarcely protect his own country from the house of Danishmend,
especially from Ya'qub Arslan,
Nur al-Din went against Farzaman and against 'Aintab,
and took them without a battle.
And in this year,
which is the year 549
[549] of the Arabs,
Nur al-Din took Damascus.
